[Pedagogy audit v2 · New question to decide] For the type count gap (summary-stats-calc). Comparison score 25, between p63-q2-block and p64-q6: Direct calculation of mean, median and range from seven unordered values. The odd count means no averaging for the median, and there is no comparison or interpretation. This is slightly easier than p64-q6.
Proposed question: Here are the numbers of runs Tom scored in his last seven cricket innings.

$12$, $35$, $8$, $35$, $20$, $41$, $10$
a) Find Tom's mean score.
b) Find the median of Tom's scores.
c) Find the range of Tom's scores.
Answers: a) $23$ runs; b) $20$ runs; c) $33$ runs

[Pedagogy audit v2 · New question to decide] For the type count gap (summary-stats-calc). Comparison score 25, between p63-q2-block and p64-q6: Median of an even-sized unordered set, mode, and a non-integer mean. These are routine procedures with no interpretation, so it is a little easier than p64-q6, which also compares the mean and median.
Proposed question: Here are the maximum temperatures recorded in Alice Springs over eight days.

$31\,^\circ\text{C}$, $34\,^\circ\text{C}$, $29\,^\circ\text{C}$, $36\,^\circ\text{C}$, $35\,^\circ\text{C}$, $38\,^\circ\text{C}$, $35\,^\circ\text{C}$, $32\,^\circ\text{C}$
a) Find the median temperature.
b) Find the mode of the temperatures.
c) Find the mean temperature.
Answers: a) $34.5\,^\circ\text{C}$; b) $35\,^\circ\text{C}$; c) $33.75\,^\circ\text{C}$

[Pedagogy audit v2 · New question to decide] For the type count gap (design-neutral-question). Comparison score 36, between p94-q5-block and p94-q4-block: Students identify leading wording ("delicious") and one-sided response options. They then write a neutral question and a balanced response scale of their own. The design part is open-ended, but a model is supplied by the earlier survey items and there is only one flaw to repair.
Proposed question: [object Object]
a) Write down one criticism of the question.
b) Suggest more suitable wording for the question.
Design a response section for your question.
Answers: a) The word “delicious” is a leading word that encourages a favourable answer. (Also acceptable: every response choice is favourable, so there is no way to give a negative answer.); b) Example: How much do you enjoy the food at the school canteen?

Tick one: Enjoy it a lot; Enjoy it a little; Neither enjoy nor dislike it; Dislike it a little; Dislike it a lot.
